evidence_legend.published: Claim or measurement reported by the project/model author; not independently reproduced here.
evidence_legend.local_measured: Measured from the checked-out/downloaded artifacts in this worktree.
evidence_legend.downstream_measured: Measurement reported by an independent downstream implementation; useful evidence, but not an upstream benchmark.
evidence_legend.not_reported: No defensible value found in the checked primary sources reviewed.

candidates.architecture: RepViT-style vision encoder (ONNX) feeding a BERT/Transformer-style autoregressive decoder (ONNX init + step); 9,415-token vocabulary.

size.detail: encoder 17,070,003 B; decoder_init 24,875,052 B; decoder_step 22,776,797 B; vocab 37,193 B

candidates.runtime: ONNX Runtime-compatible; static 1x3x224x224 encoder and batch-1 decoder graphs; autoregressive KV-cache decode.
candidates.batchability: Static batch 1 in the inspected graphs; multi-crop batching would require re-export/rewrite. Decoder remains token-step sequential per crop.
candidates.gpu_npu: Potentially portable through ONNX execution providers/delegates, but no Android GPU/NPU result was published in the reviewed sources.
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 on the Hugging Face repository.
candidates.activity: Hugging Face repository: 10 commits, one contributor, 64.8 MB total at review time.
candidates.android: Best immediate artifact candidate: small, split ONNX graphs and a compact RepViT encoder. Risks are missing model metadata, no published quality/latency benchmark, and autoregressive decoder delegate support.

candidates.architecture: Canonical Manga OCR Vision Encoder-Decoder converted to quantized ONNX and LiteRT/TFLite artifacts; repository also contains a manga text detector.

size.detail: quantized encoder 89.3 MB + quantized decoder 29.6 MB; mangaocr.tflite 113 MB

candidates.runtime: Quantized ONNX or TFLite/LiteRT; model card exposes preprocessed and quantized variants.
candidates.batchability: not_reported; artifacts are packaged for Android inference, but no batching contract is documented.
candidates.gpu_npu: TFLite/LiteRT gives a plausible NNAPI/GPU delegate path; actual delegate coverage and speed were not reported.
candidates.license: Repository page does not state a separate model license; upstream Manga OCR is Apache-2.0. Verify redistribution terms before shipping.
candidates.activity: Hugging Face repository: 13 commits, one contributor; crawled two weeks before review.
candidates.android: Most Android-oriented packaging found: includes an OCR TFLite file plus quantized ONNX, but lacks reproducible accuracy and device latency evidence.

candidates.architecture: Vision Encoder-Decoder Manga OCR export based on kha-white/manga-ocr and the manga-ocr-base-2025 fine-tune.

size.detail: encoder 22.4 MB + decoder 118 MB, plus tokenizer/configuration

candidates.runtime: ONNX Runtime via Optimum; autoregressive generation.
candidates.accuracy: not_reported for this export; upstream model describes manga-specific robustness but gives no numeric benchmark in the reviewed card.
candidates.batchability: Transformers/Optimum generation can accept batches in principle; no Android batching or fixed-shape contract is documented.
candidates.gpu_npu: ONNX execution-provider path is plausible; no mobile GPU/NPU measurement found.
candidates.license: Not stated on the l0wgear model card; source Manga OCR and manga-ocr-base-2025 are Apache-2.0, but the export should be reviewed separately.
candidates.activity: Hugging Face repository: 4 commits, one contributor, 3,361 downloads in the last month at review time.
candidates.android: A useful accuracy/reference baseline, but roughly 2.2x the inspected mobile export and not packaged as LiteRT/TFLite.

candidates.architecture: DINOv2 vision encoder (86M) plus a custom 6-layer grouped-query/SwiGLU/RMSNorm decoder; character-level 14,630-symbol vocabulary; Japanese, Chinese, and English.

size.detail: smallest shipped ONNX tier: int4 vision + int8 decoder; lossless tier 242 MB

candidates.runtime: ONNX Runtime with a KV-cache decode loop; one speech-bubble crop in, text out.
candidates.accuracy: Published model-card measurements on held-out data: Manga109-v2026 Japanese lCER 0.0345 / nCER 0.0871; exact-match 0.85 Chinese and 0.82 English on hand-annotated held-out crops. These are author-reported measurements, not independently reproduced here.
candidates.batchability: Crop-level and detector-dependent; model card documents a decode loop but no batch API/throughput claim for Android.
candidates.gpu_npu: ONNX is portable, but int4 weight-only vision and custom decoder ops need delegate validation; no Android GPU/NPU result found.
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 for weights and code per model card.
candidates.activity: Hugging Face repository: 11 commits, one contributor, 11 likes; public release includes training and quantization notes.
candidates.android: Strong quality/size candidate for a multilingual crop pipeline, but 121 MB is larger than the mobile export and it requires reliable detector crops; no Android package is published.

candidates.architecture: Approximately 150M parameters: SigLIP2 NaFlex vision encoder (~86M), projector, and 12-layer custom causal decoder (~60M), with 2D multimodal RoPE and grouped-query attention; Japanese, Chinese, Korean, and English.

size.detail: model card reports ~150M parameters and ~300 MB FP16 VRAM; public HF artifact is F32 safetensors

candidates.runtime: Transformers with trust_remote_code; crop-level generation, no separate detector. PyPI wrapper exposes runtime int4 quantization, but an Android export was not found.
candidates.accuracy: Published model-card JMangaBench_Mixed measurement: CER 3.225% and exact match 79.671% for v2.1; L4 throughput 54.22 FPS on the author's private CJK pretraining split. Author-reported, not independently reproduced here.
candidates.batchability: Author reports batching-related throughput gains; no Android batch contract. NaFlex variable patch counts complicate fixed-shape mobile delegates.
candidates.gpu_npu: GPU path is demonstrated on CUDA/L4; custom remote-code attention and NaFlex make NNAPI/NPU/LiteRT conversion uncertain.
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 on the Hugging Face model card.
candidates.activity: Hugging Face model: 7 likes, 2,371 downloads last month at review time; model card updated recently and has custom code.
candidates.android: Promising future multilingual quality candidate, not an immediate drop-in: F32/custom-code distribution, no ONNX/TFLite artifact, and only crop-level input.

candidates.architecture: 48px RGB input; ResNet feature extractor (320 channels) plus three Transformer encoder layers and CTC character head; color prediction head is also present.
candidates.runtime: Source implementation chunks text regions in batches of at most 16 and pads widths per chunk; downstream Android implementation uses ONNX Runtime.
candidates.accuracy: No numeric upstream benchmark found. The upstream issue tracker records a user report that 48px_ctc is much faster but less accurate than 48px. Downstream Yakuyomi reports 96.7% CTC parity versus FP32 after dynamic int8 quantization; this is downstream evidence, not an upstream guarantee.
candidates.batchability: Good: explicit max_chunk_size=16 and shared padded widths in the source.
candidates.gpu_npu: PyTorch source supports CUDA/MPS/XPU; Yakuyomi reports CPU MLAS because XNNPACK miscomputed this model and no GPU/NPU path was validated.
candidates.license: GPL-3.0 for manga-image-translator and the reviewed ONNX model repository.
candidates.activity: Mature upstream manga-image-translator project; the ONNX packaging repository has 5 commits and explicitly verifies max_diff=0.002 for its CTC export.
candidates.android: Most credible production reference because Yakuyomi ships an arm64 Android engine and reports ~3.6x ARM speedup and 96.7% parity after int8 quantization. GPL-3.0 and the known speed/accuracy tradeoff are material constraints.
